examples.en: I'm so sleepy that my eyes keep going heavy.

examples.ko: 동생이 잠에서 막 깨서 눈이 게슴츠레해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling just woke up, and their eyes are half-closed and dull.
He looked at me with his eyes half open.
Your eyes look heavy, as if you stayed up all night.

examples.ko: 고양이가 게슴츠레한 눈으로 창밖을 보고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is looking out the window with drowsy eyes.

examples.ko: 낮잠에서 깬 아이가 게슴츠레한 얼굴로 걸어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The child who woke from a nap came out with a drowsy face.

explain: 주로 '눈이' 뒤에 써서 졸리거나 피곤해서 눈이 반쯤 풀린 모습을 나타내요. '눈을 게슴츠레하게 뜨다'처럼 '-게' 형태로도 자주 써요. 눈 모양을 생생하게 보여 주는 말이라 기운 없고 흐릿한 눈빛에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used after '눈이' to describe eyes that are half-closed and unfocused from sleepiness or tiredness. The '-게' form is also common, as in '눈을 게슴츠레하게 뜨다'. It paints a vivid picture of the eyes, so it suits a dull, listless look.

examples.en: There is a big flagpole on the school playground.
Every morning they raise the Korean flag on the flagpole.

examples.ko: 바람이 세서 게양대의 깃발이 심하게 흔들려요.
examples.en: The wind is strong, so the flag on the flagpole is flapping hard.
Let's meet in front of the flagpole at the park entrance.

examples.ko: 새로 만든 게양대는 높이가 십 미터쯤 돼요.
examples.en: The newly built flagpole is about ten meters tall.

examples.ko: 국경일에는 관공서 게양대마다 국기가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: On national holidays, a flag hangs on every flagpole at government offices.

explain: 국기나 깃발을 다는 기둥이에요. '깃대'라고도 해요. '게양'이 국기를 높이 단다는 말이라서 '국기 게양대'처럼 국기와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is the pole on which a national flag or other flag is hung. People also say '깃대'. Because '게양' is about raising a flag high, you often see it as '국기 게양대'.

examples.en: I threw up everything I ate yesterday.
The baby drank milk and then spit up a little.

examples.ko: 차를 오래 타서 속이 안 좋아 결국 게웠어요.
examples.en: I rode in the car for a long time, felt sick, and finally threw up.

examples.ko: 속이 울렁거려서 화장실에서 다 게워 냈어요.
examples.en: My stomach was churning, so I threw it all up in the bathroom.
If your stomach hurts, don't force yourself to throw up.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 먹으면 게울 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat too much, you might throw up.

explain: '토하다'와 같은 상황에 쓰지만 '토하다'가 더 일상적이고, '게우다'는 먹은 것을 입으로 도로 내보낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 'ㅜ'가 '워'로 바뀌어 '게워요, 게웠어요'가 되고, '게워 내다'처럼도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes the same situation as '토하다', but '토하다' is more common in daily speech, while '게우다' feels like bringing back up what you ate. The stem changes to '게워요/게웠어요', and it is often used as '게워 내다'.

examples.en: In winter, the sharp drop in customers makes things hard for the shop.

examples.ko: 출산율 격감이 큰 사회 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: The sharp fall in the birth rate is becoming a big social problem.
I'm very worried because of the sharp drop in sales.

examples.ko: 수출 격감은 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
examples.en: A sharp drop in exports often comes up in economic news.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 인구 격감에 시청이 대책을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The city hall is looking for measures against the sudden sharp fall in population.

examples.ko: 판매량의 격감을 막기 위해 할인 행사를 해요.
examples.en: They are holding a sale to stop sales volume from plunging.

explain: '급감'과 거의 같아요. 숫자나 양이 갑자기 크게 줄 때 쓰고, 매출·인구·수출 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '급증'이에요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '급감'. It is used when a number or amount suddenly drops a lot, and goes well with words like sales, population and exports. The opposite is '급증'.

examples.ko: 비가 계속 오면 가게 손님이 격감해요.
examples.en: If it keeps raining, customers at the shop drop sharply.
This year's sales plunged compared with last year.

examples.ko: 인구가 격감하면 학교도 문을 닫아야 해요.
examples.en: If the population plummets, schools also have to close.
My income dropped sharply, so I'm worried about living costs.
The number of visitors is expected to fall sharply.
Let's find out why the number of tourists suddenly plummeted.

explain: '수가 격감하다'처럼 줄어드는 것을 주어로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 줄다', '많이 줄다'라고 하고, '격감하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '급증하다'예요.
explain_en: The thing that decreases is the subject, as in '수가 격감하다'. In daily talk people say '확 줄다' or '많이 줄다', while '격감하다' appears more in news and writing. The opposite is '급증하다'.

examples.en: This international competition is held every other year.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 축제는 격년제라서 올해는 없어요.
examples.en: Our school festival is held every other year, so there isn't one this year.
It's a biennial event, so it won't be held next year.

examples.ko: 박람회를 격년제에서 매년 하는 것으로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: They changed the fair from every other year to every year.

examples.ko: 이 상은 격년제여서 이 년에 한 번 줘요.
examples.en: This prize is biennial, so it's given once every two years.
Some companies have health checkups every other year.

explain: '격년'은 한 해를 거른다는 뜻이라, 격년제는 이 년에 한 번 하는 방식이에요. '격년제로 열리다/하다/운영하다'처럼 써요. 반대로 매년 하는 건 '매년'이고, 하루 걸러 하는 건 '격일제'예요.
explain_en: '격년' means skipping a year, so '격년제' is a system of doing something once every two years. It is used as '격년제로 열리다/하다/운영하다'. Doing it every year is '매년', and every other day is '격일제'.

examples.en: The boss found out about the mistake and was furious.
Citizens were enraged by the unfair result.
My father heard the lie and flew into a rage.
The players were furious at the referee's call and protested.

examples.ko: 그렇게 격노할 일은 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think it's something to get so enraged about.
The news showed the fans in a rage.

explain: '화나다'보다 훨씬 강하고 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 글에서 많이 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '엄청 화났어요'처럼 말해요. 높일 때는 '격노하셨어요'처럼 '-시-'를 넣어요.
explain_en: It is much stronger and more formal than '화나다', so you see it often in news and writing. In everyday talk people say things like '엄청 화났어요'. To show respect, add '-시-', as in '격노하셨어요'.

examples.en: My grandfather is someone who lived through turbulent times.

examples.ko: 그 시절은 사회가 크게 흔들린 격동기였어요.
examples.en: That time was a turbulent period when society was shaken greatly.
In turbulent times, people's thinking changes quickly too.

examples.ko: 격동기의 한국을 다룬 드라마를 보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm watching a drama about Korea in a turbulent era.

examples.ko: 정치적 격동기 속에서 많은 일이 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: Many things happened during the political upheaval.
It's an economically turbulent period, so investing is hard.

explain: '격변기'와 거의 비슷하게 써요. '격동기'는 흔들리고 요동치는 느낌이 있고, '격변기'는 크게 바뀐다는 느낌이 있어요. '격동기를 거치다/살다'처럼 시대 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used almost like '격변기'. '격동기' feels like things being shaken and churned, while '격변기' feels like things changing greatly. It often appears in talk about eras, as in '격동기를 거치다/살다'.

examples.en: The ship was caught in heavy seas and rocked hard.
The sea turned rough because of the typhoon.
The fishermen came back through the raging waves.

examples.ko: 경제가 격랑 속에 빠졌다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the economy has fallen into turmoil.
The political world is being pulled into turmoil.

examples.ko: 인생의 격랑은 누구나 한 번쯤 겪어요.
examples.en: Everyone goes through life's storms at least once.

explain: 바다의 사납고 큰 물결인데, 사회·정치·인생의 큰 혼란을 빗대어 쓰는 일이 많아요. '격랑에 휩쓸리다', '격랑 속에서'처럼 자주 같이 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means large, fierce waves at sea, but it is often used figuratively for great turmoil in society, politics or life. It commonly appears as '격랑에 휩쓸리다' or '격랑 속에서'. You see it more in news and writing than in daily talk.

examples.en: The two teams clashed fiercely in the final.
Citizens strongly opposed that decision.
The child cried so hard that it was difficult to calm him.

examples.ko: 격렬히 운동한 뒤에는 물을 충분히 마셔요.
examples.en: After intense exercise, I drink enough water.
The two of them debated heatedly for a long time.
The workers protested vehemently to the boss.

explain: '격렬하게'와 같은 뜻이지만 '격렬히'가 조금 더 글 느낌이에요. 운동, 싸움, 토론, 반대처럼 행동이나 감정이 아주 세고 거칠 때 써요. 조용하거나 부드러운 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It means the same as '격렬하게', but '격렬히' sounds a bit more like written language. It is used when actions or feelings are very strong and intense, such as exercise, fights, debates and opposition. It doesn't fit calm or gentle situations.

examples.en: I suffered from a heavy workload and my health got much worse.
My father is always tired because of his heavy workload.
A colleague who collapsed from overwork was admitted to the hospital.

examples.ko: 요즘 격무가 계속돼서 주말에도 쉬지 못해요.
examples.en: The heavy workload continues these days, so I can't rest even on weekends.
The workload was too much to bear, so I moved to another department.

examples.ko: 병원 의사들은 격무 속에서도 환자를 먼저 생각해요.
examples.en: Hospital doctors put patients first even amid a heavy workload.

explain: 일이 많고 힘든 직장 생활에 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '일이 너무 많아요'라고 하고, '격무'는 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. '격무에 시달리다'로 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for a job with a lot of hard work. In daily talk people say '일이 너무 많아요', while '격무' shows up more in news and writing. The most common pattern is '격무에 시달리다'.

examples.ko: 조선 말기는 사회가 크게 바뀐 격변기였어요.
examples.en: The late Joseon period was an age of great upheaval.

examples.ko: 격변기에 태어난 세대는 생각이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: The generation born in a time of upheaval thinks very differently.
Now is a period of upheaval, with technology changing fast.
I listened to the story of my grandmother, who lived through an era of upheaval.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 격변기의 위기를 잘 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our company got through the crisis of the turbulent period well.
It's a time of upheaval, so it's hard to predict the future.

explain: '격동기'와 비슷하지만 '격변기'는 세상이 크게 바뀐다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 역사, 사회, 기술 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '격변기를 맞다/겪다/지나다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '격동기', but '격변기' puts more weight on the world changing greatly. It often appears when talking about history, society and technology. It is used as '격변기를 맞다/겪다/지나다'.

examples.en: Competition for entrance exams gets more intense every year.
Traffic congestion is severe during the morning commute.

examples.ko: 격심한 통증 때문에 잠을 잘 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the severe pain.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 가격 경쟁이 격심해서 소비자는 좋아요.
examples.en: The price competition between the two companies is fierce, which is good for consumers.

examples.ko: 날씨 변화가 격심할 때는 건강을 잘 챙기세요.
examples.en: Take good care of your health when the weather changes drastically.

examples.ko: 격심하게 흔들리는 버스 안에서 멀미가 났어요.
examples.en: I got carsick on the bus that was shaking violently.

explain: '심하다'보다 더 강하고 글 말투에 가까워요. 경쟁, 고통, 변화, 피해처럼 정도가 아주 센 것과 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '너무 심해요'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '심하다' and closer to written style. It goes well with things of very high degree, such as competition, pain, change and damage. In daily conversation people more often just say '너무 심해요'.

examples.en: We are on such close terms that we talk without reserve.

examples.ko: 선배가 격의 없는 태도로 저를 대해 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior treated me in a friendly, unreserved way.

examples.ko: 서로 격의 없어서 같이 있으면 편해요.
examples.en: We're so open with each other that it's comfortable to be together.

examples.ko: 앞으로는 격의 없게 지내자고 먼저 말했어요.
examples.en: I was the first to say that we should be casual with each other from now on.

examples.ko: 우리 사이에 격의 없다고 생각해서 솔직히 말했어요.
examples.en: I thought we had no need for formality between us, so I spoke honestly.
We're comfortable with each other now, so please speak freely.

explain: 거의 '격의 없다/없이'의 모양으로만 써요. 사이가 가까워서 어려워하거나 예의를 너무 차리지 않아도 되는 관계에 쓰고, 좋은 뜻이에요. '격의 없이 지내다/대하다/말하다'가 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '격의 없다/없이'. It describes a close relationship where you don't have to be shy or overly formal, and it has a positive meaning. Common patterns are '격의 없이 지내다/대하다/말하다'.

examples.en: The security guards at our company work every other day.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 격일제라서 하루 걸러 가요.
examples.en: This class runs every other day, so I go every second day.

examples.ko: 격일제 근무는 하루 일하고 하루 쉬어요.
examples.en: With an every-other-day schedule, you work one day and rest the next.

examples.ko: 제가 격일제를 선택한 이유는 시간이 자유롭기 때문이에요.
examples.en: The reason I chose the every-other-day system is that my time is free.

examples.ko: 근무 방식이 격일제에서 매일 출근으로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The work system changed from every other day to daily attendance.
Many people say the every-other-day system is tough.

explain: '격일'은 하루를 거른다는 뜻이라, 격일제는 하루 걸러 하루 일하거나 운영하는 방식이에요. 근무나 수업, 운영 방식을 말할 때 써요. 한 해 걸러 하는 방식은 '격년제'예요.
explain_en: '격일' means skipping a day, so '격일제' is a system of working or operating every other day. It is used for work shifts, classes and operating schedules. Doing something every other year is '격년제'.

examples.en: The two teams fought a fierce battle in the final.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기는 격전이 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: Today's match looks like it will be a fierce fight.
Our team won after a hard-fought battle.
This tournament was one fierce battle after another.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 선거 때마다 격전으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That district is famous for fierce contests at every election.
The fierce battle continued until late at night.

explain: 치열하게 맞붙는 싸움을 말하고, 실제 전투뿐 아니라 스포츠나 선거 같은 경쟁에도 비유로 써요. '격전을 벌이다/치르다'처럼 자주 써요. 가벼운 다툼에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It refers to a fiercely contested fight, and besides real battles it is also used figuratively for competition such as sports and elections. It commonly appears as '격전을 벌이다/치르다'. It is not used for minor quarrels.

examples.en: This region is counted as a key battleground in the election.

examples.ko: 역사책에 나온 유명한 격전지를 찾아가 봤어요.
examples.en: I visited a famous battle site mentioned in history books.
That island was a fiercely fought battleground long ago.
A memorial hall stands at the battle site now.
The candidates go from one battleground district to another campaigning.
The scenery of the old battleground is very peaceful now.

explain: 원래는 치열한 전투가 벌어진 곳이고, 선거 뉴스에서는 누가 이길지 알기 어려운 지역을 '격전지'라고 해요. '선거 격전지'가 자주 쓰이는 말이에요.
explain_en: Originally it means a place where fierce fighting took place, and in election news it also refers to a district where the winner is hard to predict. '선거 격전지' is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 격정적인 무대에 관객이 환호했어요.
examples.en: The audience cheered for the singer's passionate performance.

examples.ko: 영화에서 두 사람의 격정적인 사랑이 그려져요.
examples.en: The film portrays the passionate love of the two people.

examples.ko: 격정적 감정을 글로 풀어 쓰면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Writing out intense emotions makes you feel better.
The musician played the piano passionately.
His way of speaking is always impassioned.
The speech was so emotional that I cried.

explain: 감정이 세게 터져 나오는 모습을 말해요. 음악, 연기, 사랑, 연설 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 보통 '격정적인 ~', '격정적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요.
explain_en: It describes emotion bursting out strongly. It goes well with music, acting, love and speeches. It is usually used in forms like '격정적인 ~' and '격정적으로'.

examples.en: Critics praised this movie highly.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 발표를 격찬해 주셔서 기뻤어요.
examples.en: I was happy that my teacher praised my presentation so highly.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 이 식당의 맛을 격찬해요.
examples.en: Many people rave about the taste of this restaurant.

examples.ko: 신문은 그 선수의 활약을 격찬하는 기사를 냈어요.
examples.en: The newspaper ran an article lavishing praise on the player's performance.

examples.ko: 외국 기자들도 한국 음식을 격찬할 정도예요.
examples.en: Even foreign reporters go so far as to praise Korean food highly.
It's a work that received high praise, so I'm looking forward to it.

explain: '칭찬하다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 아주 훌륭하다고 말할 때 써요. 영화, 책, 공연, 음식처럼 평가받는 대상에 잘 어울려요. '격찬을 받다'라는 말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '칭찬하다' and is used when saying something is truly excellent. It suits things that get reviewed, such as films, books, performances and food. '격찬을 받다' is also a common expression.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있으면 견갑골 주변이 뻐근해요.
examples.en: If I sit for a long time, the area around my shoulder blades gets stiff.
The doctor said there is a crack in my shoulder blade.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 견갑골을 모아 주는 자세가 중요해요.
examples.en: In this exercise, the posture of squeezing the shoulder blades together is important.
My shoulder blades look sticking out, and it bothers me.
Try pointing to where your shoulder blade is with your hand.
I carried a heavy bag, and even my shoulder blades hurt.

explain: 병원이나 운동 이야기에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 쉬운 우리말로는 '날개뼈'라고 해요. 등 위쪽, 어깨 뒤에 있는 뼈를 가리켜요. '견갑골 운동'처럼 헬스 이야기에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is common in talk about hospitals and exercise, and the plainer Korean word is '날개뼈'. It points to the bone at the upper back behind the shoulder. It also often appears in fitness talk, as in '견갑골 운동'.

examples.en: A bridge has to be built solidly to be safe.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 협력 관계를 견고히 다졌어요.
examples.en: The two countries firmly strengthened their cooperative relationship.
I locked the door securely and went out.

examples.ko: 건물 기초를 견고히 해야 오래 가요.
examples.en: You have to make the building's foundation solid for it to last.

examples.ko: 견고히 쌓은 신뢰는 쉽게 무너지지 않아요.
examples.en: Trust built firmly doesn't collapse easily.
I tied the luggage tightly and loaded it into the car.

explain: '단단히'와 비슷하지만 '견고히'는 글이나 격식 있는 말투에 어울려요. 건물·구조물 같은 물건뿐 아니라 관계, 신뢰, 협력에도 써요. '견고히 하다/다지다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '단단히'를 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '단단히', but '견고히' fits written or formal speech. It is used for objects like buildings and structures as well as for relationships, trust and cooperation. Common patterns are '견고히 하다/다지다', and in daily talk people more often say '단단히'.

en: seeing something makes you want it

examples.ko: 견물생심이라고, 가게에서 예쁜 걸 보니 사고 싶어졌어요.
examples.en: They say seeing breeds wanting: I saw something pretty in the shop and wanted to buy it.
Seeing makes you want things, so I left my wallet at home.
As the saying goes, once you see it you want it, and my spending goes up whenever I go to the mall.
Wanting what you see is a feeling everyone has.

examples.ko: 견물생심이 무서워서 비싼 가게는 안 가요.
examples.en: I'm afraid of wanting things when I see them, so I don't go to expensive stores.

examples.ko: 아이들은 견물생심으로 장난감 가게 앞을 못 떠나요.
examples.en: The kids want everything they see and can't leave the front of the toy store.

explain: 물건을 직접 보면 갖고 싶은 마음이 생긴다는 말이에요. 쇼핑이나 충동구매 이야기에서 가볍게 쓰고, '견물생심이라고'처럼 인용하는 모양으로 자주 말해요. 영어의 'opportunity makes the thief'와 완전히 같지는 않고, 보면 욕심이 생긴다는 쪽에 가까워요.
explain_en: It says that when you actually see something, you start to want it. It is used lightly in talk about shopping and impulse buying, often in a quoting form like '견물생심이라고'. It is not exactly the same as 'opportunity makes the thief'; it is closer to 'seeing it makes you want it'.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 달부터 병원에서 견습을 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started my apprenticeship at a hospital this month.
The pay is a bit lower during the training period.

examples.ko: 지금은 견습 중이라 모르는 게 많아요.
examples.en: I'm still in training, so there's a lot I don't know.

examples.ko: 견습이 끝나면 정식 직원이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: When the apprenticeship ends, you can become a regular employee.
He learned the work as an apprentice at a hair salon.
She started as a trainee and is now a team leader.

explain: 직업을 배우는 중인 사람이나 그 기간에 쓰는 말이에요. '견습 사원', '견습 기간'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙는 일이 많아요. '수습'과 비슷한 자리에서 쓰지만, '견습'은 보고 배운다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who is learning a trade, or to that period. It often comes before other words, as in '견습 사원' and '견습 기간'. It is used in similar places as '수습', but '견습' has a stronger feel of learning by watching.
